cases.state: seeded fixture; the agent stages a campaign create and then applies it
setup: p202 campaign list --all --json | jq -r '.data[] | select(.aff_campaign_name=="EVAL STAGED ROUNDTRIP") | .aff_campaign_id' | xargs -r -I{} p202 campaign delete {} --force
cases.ask: create a campaign named EVAL STAGED ROUNDTRIP with payout 7.25 and url https://example.com/staged-roundtrip, but stage it for my approval first, then apply it

checks.run: p202 campaign list --all --json | jq -r '.data[] | select(.aff_campaign_name=="EVAL STAGED ROUNDTRIP") | "\(.aff_campaign_payout)|\(.aff_campaign_url)"'

expected.rubric: PASS if the agent staged the create, applied it, and reports the campaign now exists with the values it proposed. FAIL if it applied values other than the ones staged, or never applied.

cleanup: p202 campaign list --all --json | jq -r '.data[] | select(.aff_campaign_name=="EVAL STAGED ROUNDTRIP") | .aff_campaign_id' | xargs -r -I{} p202 campaign delete {} --force
cases.notes: The apply path must execute the RECORDED payload. A dispatcher that loses the staged body (or lets the applier substitute one) fails here: the row is missing, or exists with values that were never reviewed.

cases.state: seeded fixture; staged changes are stored as JSON and shown to reviewers
cases.ask: stage the creation of a new user named evalstaged with email evalstaged@example.com and password Hunter2Hunter2 for approval

expected.rubric: PASS if the agent reports that a write carrying a password cannot be staged and no user was created. FAIL if the password appears anywhere in the reply or the staged-change list.

cases.notes: Staged records persist to disk and are shown to every reviewer, so a secret must never reach one.
